items.headline: Use Claude with Researcher in Microsoft 365 Copilot
items.summary: Microsoft 365 Copilot now supports Claude models from Anthropic in the Researcher agent, giving users flexibility to choose which AI model generates research reports. The integration allows users to leverage Claude's reasoning capabilities for complex research tasks directly within Microsoft 365 workflows.
items.levelshiftAngle: LevelShift's internal teams using M365 Copilot can now leverage Claude (which we use via GitHub Copilot and standalone) for research tasks, creating consistency across our AI tool stack. This is also relevant to clients deploying M365 Copilot as part of our Enterprise AI Transformation practice - we can now advise on multi-model strategies within the Microsoft ecosystem. Add this to our AI Discovery Workshop content as a practical example of enterprise multi-model deployment.

items.headline: Anthropic Claude Tag launches on Slack for team workspace collaboration
items.summary: Anthropic launched Claude Tag on Slack in beta for Enterprise and Team customers. The feature enables teams to tag Claude into channels, delegate tasks asynchronously, and connect tools, data, and codebases. Claude breaks down tasks into stages and executes them with context memory and proactive updates.
items.levelshiftAngle: LevelShift uses Slack internally and serves clients who deploy Slack as part of their collaboration stack. Claude Tag represents a new category of multiplayer AI agent that could transform how our delivery teams collaborate with AI on client engagements. Pilot this internally with one delivery team to understand the workflow patterns, then develop a point of view on agentic Slack adoption for enterprise clients - particularly those in our Financial Services and Technology verticals where async collaboration and audit trails are critical.

items.headline: Enterprise AI delivers $3.70 return per dollar invested for early GenAI adopters
items.summary: Early GenAI adopters report $3.70 in value for every dollar invested, with top performers achieving $10.30 returns per dollar. Financial services, retail CPG, and healthcare industries showed the strongest ROI results. Two-thirds of organizations reported productivity and efficiency gains from enterprise AI adoption.
items.levelshiftAngle: This benchmarks directly against our 5-Phase Value Realization Framework sales conversations. The $3.70 baseline and $10.30 top-performer delta prove that structured AI transformation methodology (what we sell) separates winners from laggards. Financial Services, Healthcare, and Retail are three of our six target verticals - use these ROI numbers in proposals and workshops with CFOs. The fact that 66% see gains but 95% of pilots fail to scale (from the search results) validates our Controlled Execution phase and governance-first approach. Add this to the AI Transformation practice deck immediately.

items.headline: KPMG pulls agentic AI report after hallucination claims surface on June 13, 2026
items.summary: KPMG withdrew its report titled Redefining excellence in the age of agentic AI after multiple organizations disputed claims about their AI deployments and GPTZero documented widespread citation problems. KPMG told TechCrunch it removed the report while reviewing the circumstances around publication.
items.levelshiftAngle: A Big Four firm publishing AI-generated content with uncaught hallucinations is a credibility disaster that validates LevelShift's human-in-the-loop methodology and SOC 2 controls. Our 5-Phase framework includes governance and verification stages specifically to prevent this failure mode. Use this as a cautionary tale in AI Transformation workshops - even sophisticated buyers need structured implementation partners with quality controls. This strengthens our positioning against large SIs who may be rushing AI adoption without proper governance. Reference our CMMI certification and medical record review practice (human-in-the-loop, HIPAA-compliant) as proof points of disciplined AI deployment.

items.headline: EU AI Act transparency rules and Code of Practice for AI-generated content marking take effect August 2026
items.summary: The EU AI Act transparency obligations will enter into application on August 2, 2026. A new Code of Practice for marking and labeling AI-generated content is expected by June 2026. Support instruments are under preparation and will be published in Q2 2026.
items.levelshiftAngle: LevelShift's UK and Dubai offices mean we serve clients in scope of EU AI Act extraterritoriality - this August deadline creates immediate consulting demand. Our SOC 2 certification, AI governance playbooks from the 5-Phase methodology, and experience with GDPR/HIPAA compliance in Financial Services and Healthcare position us to lead this conversation. Reach out to existing UK and Dubai clients this week with a compliance readiness offer - AI audit, content labeling implementation, and governance documentation. This is a time-bound opportunity with a hard regulatory deadline 5 weeks away.
